releases.title: Attached files upload on request, and steadier answers
changes: Attach a file and send any message: the upload confirmation card appears at once, with extraction when you ask for it, instead of an explanation.
A plain question never turns into an extraction proposal, and a search that lands during re-indexing waits a few seconds instead of failing.
A total of three or four listed figures is kept in the answer, and answers quoting saved extraction values are no longer removed by the source check.

Spreadsheets: a single-row sheet and a label-and-value sheet keep their values, total rows are marked and left out of column statistics, and a template naming specific rows or whole-table figures is read by the model instead of row by row.

releases.title: Reading a document for fields asks first
changes: The template helper's "From the document" and the knowledge index Retry now show the same external-processing approval as uploads and re-extractions before any document text leaves Lapi, and say so when you decline.

releases.title: Review saves without locking
changes: Review has a Save changes button that keeps the result open, and a separate Mark reviewed button that explains the permanent lock and asks before applying it.
People with Viewer access see the values without editable fields and are told who can grant Editor access.

releases.title: Stop means stop, and a reload keeps your answer
changes: Stop now reaches the server: model and tool calls end at the next step and the partial answer is kept, instead of running on unseen.
Closing or reloading the page no longer discards an answer in progress. The answer finishes, and the page picks it up again with its progress and lets you stop it.
Stop is available from the moment you send, and a running upload or extraction workflow has a Cancel workflow action that says what is kept.

releases.title: Extraction takes a second look
changes: When a model's extraction does not match the template, Lapi tells it what was wrong and tries once more.
Fields left empty get a second look with more of the document, and a value is kept only when the model quotes it from the source.
Every file in a combined extraction now reaches the model, and files with no readable text are recorded with the result.

releases.title: English answers, calculations kept, top row found
changes: Lapi Agent always answers in English.
Calculations written with LaTeX or a discount multiplier such as × 0.85 are no longer removed.
Asking for the highest or lowest value with other columns returns that row, such as the order and customer with the highest revenue.

releases.title: Rejected sentences are removed again; month-name dates match
changes: A sentence the answer check rejects is always removed, even when its number appears in a source. In 26.1.16.49 such a sentence could stay and show a wrong answer.
Calculated results that passed the value check are no longer sent to that check, which cannot confirm them from source text.
Dates written with month names now match: March 15, 2026 agrees with a source's 15 Mar 2026.

releases.title: QA fixes: answers keep their numbers, set-up chat never traps you, uploads report per file
changes: Lapi Agent keeps correct answers: dates match by meaning (13/04/2026 is 13 April 2026), a calculation that shows its steps is accepted, table rows and summaries built from exact spreadsheet results are kept, and facts you typed in the conversation (a client name, a PO number, a correction) count as evidence. A judge's doubt no longer deletes a sentence whose values are all in its sources.
Spreadsheet questions: revenue, margin and similar figures are calculated row by row as one derived metric ("quantity * unit_price"), listed and sorted like any column.

Set-up chat: a failed extraction becomes a step with Try again or Finish for now; Close always works; each document gets its own extraction instead of one merged record; the reading counter shows the final count.

Uploading through the agent reuses the files sent with the request; a # followed by a space is ordinary text; Enter while Lapi is answering explains what to do; the account button and attachment list fit phones.
Uploads check every file on its own and report the rejected ones by name; empty and oversized files get separate messages; a model that answers 429, 502, 503 or 504 is retried twice before an error.

Workbooks: a merged title row above the header is no longer taken as the column names. Files & processing no longer flags image documents as needing a reindex when the workspace Default OCR model read them.

Dashboard counters show a dash while loading and greet you by the name you chose; Needs attention stage names are readable; the Access map describes Contributors correctly; the default "your documents" collection is reused instead of created again; Caddy sends HSTS, nosniff, frame-ancestors and referrer headers.

releases.title: Decisions checks Lapi Agent answers too
changes: The Lapi Agent's chat now checks every cited sentence with Decisions when a Decisions Default is set. Before, only the Dashboard chat and the Agent's other chat path did, so live Agent answers were never checked. Sentences Decisions rejects get one rewrite, then are removed, and the answer says how many were removed.
Set-up and Help chat: when Decisions is confident an answer matches none of the choices, such as "hi", Lapi asks again in its own words instead of passing the answer to the chat model.
Asking again in the set-up and Help chat now looks like a normal Lapi message, not an orange error.

releases.title: Answers checked against their sources
changes: Model Registration has a Decisions use for OpenAI connections. It uses OpenAI's Decisions API (gpt-6-luna), which returns probabilities and choices instead of text. Test connection asks two questions with known answers. Decisions is registered on its own and has its own optional workspace Default, with Stop using to turn it off.

With a Decisions Default, both chats check each cited sentence against the sources it cites before showing the answer. A sentence the sources do not support is sent back for one rewrite from the same evidence; if it still is not supported, the answer is not shown. The saved trace records whether the check passed, failed, was unavailable or was not set up.
Dashboard chat asks Decisions whether a question needs your knowledge before answering it directly. Decisions can only send a question to knowledge lookup; it never skips lookup.
The set-up chat reads yes, no and which-option answers with Decisions when it is set. Unclear answers go to the chat model or the screen's own rules as before.
Without a Decisions Default, every chat and the set-up chat work exactly as before.

releases.title: Lapi sets you up in a chat
changes: At first sign-in Lapi sets you up in a chat: what to call you, a team workspace if you want one, which workspace to use, and your first collection with its type. Answers can be typed, tapped or spoken.

The chat carries on through your first round: say what you want to pull out and Lapi suggests the fields, filled in from your words; change them in words; take a photo or choose files; Lapi asks before reading them, reads, extracts and shows the first results, with Review one tap away.

Behind the chat, the overall Default chat model reads what you type or say: it fixes typos in your name, understands yes and no in your own words, turns a plain sentence into fields, and asks again kindly when an answer does not fit. Without a chat model the built-in rules still work.
Your personal workspace and the greeting use the name you gave.
Quick Extract on phones opens straight on your documents, with a scan-style photo tile, the collection as a chip you can change, a reading ring and fields as chips.

In the Agent, when a request needs a prompt template and there is none, Lapi helps on the spot: say what to pull out and it fills in the fields (or reads the document), lets you change them in words, and saves them as the template.

A Help tab at the bottom of the phone screen, and Help from Lapi at the bottom of the side menu: tap any time to add a collection, make a team workspace, pull out data, or email Mani for help with the details filled in. Error messages offer the same email.

Two marks: the Agent is the Reader spark, a page whose lines light up as an orange spark reads down them and flares when the answer is ready; Help is a friendly robot that blinks, waves and holds a question bubble. Both in the phone tab bar and the side menu, still for anyone with reduced motion on.

releases.title: Private workspaces and a calmer phone
changes: Your personal workspace is yours alone: nobody else sees it, whatever their role. Administrators and contributors open only the collections they created or were given.
On phones the top row holds just the workspace name, a dot for files that need you, and your account. Chat greets you by name with three big starters, and the collection chip opens the chat options.
Quick Extract shows what it found as figures first. The tab bar floats above the screen edge.
Your question in chat keeps its own width on the right.

releases.title: Workspaces hold collections
changes: A workspace now holds document collections, and each collection can have a type such as Finance or Resume.
When you sign in, Lapi asks which workspace you want. If you have none, it guides you through creating one and a first collection.
Team workspace members see every collection in it. Files, Review, Extract and prompts follow the open workspace.
Everyone can create one personal and one team workspace, and can join other people's. Administrators have no limit.
Existing collections keep their access: unshared ones go to their owner's personal workspace, shared ones to an Organization workspace.
Connections, version and privacy moved behind the i button so chat has more room, and text sizes follow the screen.

releases.title: Workspaces
changes: Datasets are now called workspaces everywhere you see them. Manage workspace is now Settings, and the workspace Default model is now the overall Default.
If you have no workspace when you sign in, Lapi asks you to create one, for just you or for your team. For a team you add people straight away; they need a Lapi account first.
Anyone can create a workspace and owns what they create: one personal and one team. Administrators have no limit. Personal workspaces cannot be shared.
The Agent says workspace and understands it when you type it.

releases.title: Signing in starts fresh
changes: Signing out and signing in with a username and password now reload the page, so you get the latest release and a fresh chat. Saved conversations stay in History.
Signing out also clears the tab's saved chat data, including for company sign-in.

releases.title: A calmer Agent
changes: Lapi Agent now opens with a short greeting and four suggestions, on phones and computers. The explanation, workflow cards and extra chips are gone.
Typing / or # still brings up commands and documents, and What can you do? opens the full guide.
On phones, foldables and tablets, status is one row of short labels.

releases.title: Foldables and tablets get the phone layout
changes: Touch screens up to 1100 pixels wide, such as foldables and tablets, now open on Lapi Agent with the Agent and Quick Extract tabs, and use the models offered on phones.
Computers without touch keep their layout, even in a narrow window.

releases.title: Phones: Agent and Quick Extract
changes: Phones now open on Lapi Agent with two tabs, Agent and Quick Extract. The Dashboard is no longer shown on phones; More stays for people with other screens.
Quick Extract goes straight to pulling out data from your documents.
On phones, a short status line replaces the floating progress card, and the chat box takes less room.
Calculated answers lead with the number and show how your question was read, taken from the calculation that ran.
Spreadsheet sources open with Source, Row, Attached and Linked tabs, and amounts that disagree are flagged.
Review moves through results one record at a time, with Previous and Next, or a swipe on phones.

releases.title: Different models for phones and computers
changes: In Manage workspace > Enabled models, each model has Phone and Computer toggles: offer it on phones, computers or both, so small models can serve phones and large ones computers. Models start on both.
Lapi Agent, the Dashboard chat and Quick start list only the chat models offered on the device in use, and switch when the window crosses the phone width.
The choice stays when a model's connection is edited in Model Registration.

releases.title: Choose and switch models from a phone
changes: Administrators have a new Enabled models screen under Manage workspace, on phones and computers: one switch per registered model to offer it for chat and new work or not, without editing its connection. A workspace Default stays on until another Default is chosen.
On phones, the chat box shows the Agent Model picker on its own labelled row. It lists only models that are on and says where to turn one on when none is.

releases.title: A phone design that puts the answer first
changes: On phones, Home opens on one ask box with suggested questions from your newest files, then what needs you (files that failed) and what Lapi is still reading, with its step and progress.
The phone tab bar is Home, Ask, a raised Add button in the middle, Review and More.
Chat on phones shows your question in a dark bubble and the answer on a card; sources and follow-up questions are large chips, and a source opens as a sheet from the bottom.
When Quick start checks your spreadsheet columns, each field shows how its column was chosen: same name, by meaning, linked sheet, AI per row or no column.
On phones, Review keeps its save and approve buttons large and at the bottom. Computers are unchanged.

releases.title: Workbooks: everything read and connected
changes: Lapi now reads every part of an Excel workbook: formulas (and calculates results Excel never saved), comments, links, highlights, hidden rows, images (read by the AI vision model), charts, text boxes and embedded files. Anything it cannot read is listed with the reason, never skipped silently.

Each part is tied to its sheet, cell and row, and the links are recorded: formula sources, keys shared between sheets (Transactions to Vendors), chart data ranges, and receipts or files that belong to a row, with amounts that disagree flagged.

Extraction from spreadsheets matches your fields to columns by meaning (Invoice number to Reference No, Vendor country through the Vendors sheet), checks every match, and lets you confirm or change it in Quick start before it runs.
Fields that are not columns, such as text on a receipt image or a comment, are read by the AI row by row in small batches, so large sheets never exceed the model's limit.
In chat, the agent understands what each column and value means, joins linked sheets for exact numbers, and can start from an image or an invoice number to reach everything connected to it.

releases.title: Spreadsheets are extracted row by row
changes: When the fields you ask for are columns of a spreadsheet (Transaction ID, Date, Amount...), Lapi now reads every row straight from the table: one record per row, exact values, no AI model call and no size limit.
This fixes extractions on large spreadsheets that stopped with "Selected content exceeds this model's context budget".
Fields that match no column are left empty and named in the review note. Quick start shows the first record and how many there are; Review opens on the first row.

releases.title: Clearer extraction failures in Quick start
changes: When an extraction stops, the reason is shown at the top of the step instead of below the screen.
The red cross now sits on the step that actually failed (for example reading with the AI model), not always on "Waiting for a worker".
If an extraction takes longer than 10 minutes, Quick start says it is still running and where to check it, instead of saying it stopped.

releases.title: The tour is a motion video
changes: The one-minute tour is now one continuous motion video with a natural voice and soft music, instead of scene-by-scene cards: documents flow into the knowledge base, a question is answered with sources, fields are pulled out and reviewed, a skill takes effect, and it ends on Quick start.
Play, pause, sound on/off, a progress bar, captions, and Go to Dashboard or Replay at the end. People who prefer reduced motion keep the scene player.

releases.title: Skills that apply themselves
changes: A skill can say when it applies: document types, domains, keywords or specific documents. The agent then uses it by itself whenever a request or document matches, and says which skill it used.
Upload a skill as a SKILL.md file (front matter + steps) in Skills & memory, and download any skill to share it. Uploading a name you already have replaces your skill.
The built-in invoice-review skill is the example: it applies to invoices, bills and receipts.
The tour has a new Skills scene and the agent training a new card, so everyone sees how skills work.

releases.title: The agent guides plain requests end to end
changes: Type what you want in plain words ("upload this one", "pull out the totals", "create a dataset", "write a prompt", "start") and the agent leads you through what is missing: attach the document, pick or create a dataset, draft a prompt, with one next-step button each. Your words stay in the box so you can send again when ready.
A guided start can begin with the documents you already attached in the agent.
When nothing is missing, such a request runs the real workflow directly instead of being guessed at by the model.
The sign-in page artwork no longer repeats Connect, Unify, Ask under the title.

releases.title: Dense pages are read in parts
changes: A scanned page with more text than the OCR model can return in one answer is read in parts, decided before the model is asked. Cuts fall in gaps between sections, never through a line or a table, and each part knows how the one above ended so tables keep their columns.
While this happens the progress line says why it is taking longer ("Page 3 has a lot of text: reading it in parts…").
The remaining OCR message is in plain words and says what to do.

releases.title: Sign in with Google
changes: The sign-in popup shows a Sign in with Google button that goes straight to Google.
The popup no longer mentions Keycloak: it talks about your work account, Google, and a username and password.

releases.title: Agent-first phone version
changes: On phones, Lapi now shows three things: Dashboard, Lapi Agent and Quick start. Everything else runs through the agent. Administrators keep every screen on every device.

Screens are controlled from the Access map's new Screens tab: per screen, Phone and Computer, for everyone, a team, or off, with presets. Decided by OpenFGA and applied within a minute, with no deploy.
A short in-agent training (five cards with Try it buttons) shows once, and any time from the How the agent works chip.
Quick start opens from the agent (Guided start chip or /Start) and can hand back into the agent with the dataset selected.
The phone Dashboard opens with Lapi Agent as the front door; quick-action chips sit above the agent's message box.

releases.title: Spreadsheets, exact answers and charts
changes: Upload Excel (.xlsx), CSV and TSV files. Every sheet is read with its header row, real values and dates; each row is indexed with its column names, so a value never loses its column, and each sheet gets a summary. Sources show the sheet and row numbers.
Lapi Agent answers totals, averages, counts, rankings and per-month figures by calculating on the stored table, so the numbers are exact rather than estimated from text.
Ask Lapi Agent for a chart and it draws a bar, line, pie or scatter chart from that calculation, with the numbers underneath and a Download data button.
While Lapi Agent works you see a slim status line; the detailed workflow opens only when you tap it.
New releases now show straight away: the app's pages are re-checked on every visit instead of being kept from an older version.

releases.title: Roomier, easier-to-read chat
changes: Lapi Agent and the Dashboard chat use a roomy, centred reading column: your question in a soft bubble, answers as plain text in a comfortable reading font, with lists, code and source numbers laid out clearly.
While Lapi works you see what it is doing right now: understanding your question, searching your knowledge, writing the answer, checking it against its sources.
A larger rounded message box with an orange send button; the Context panel in Lapi Agent shows only on very wide screens so the conversation has room.
On phones the floating Ask button no longer covers the chat's message box.

releases.title: Voice-over and phone and computer versions of the tour
changes: The 1-minute tour (Dashboard and About) now has a voice-over: each scene's caption is spoken as it plays, with the most natural English voice on your device, and the tour waits for the voice before moving on.
A Voice on / off button in the tour, remembered on your device. When the tour opens by itself, browsers need a tap before they speak: tap Turn on voice.
The tour's lines are updated for today's Lapi (Quick start, models chosen by your administrator), so everyone sees it once more.

Two versions of the tour: on phones it shows and narrates Quick start, the Add tab, taking photos and merging pages; on computers it covers Add knowledge connectors, Lapi Agent, side-by-side review and keyboard shortcuts.

releases.title: Merge files, extraction workflow and Review from Quick start
changes: New dataset in Quick start asks for a name and an optional description.

Uploading several files, in Quick start or with /Upload in Lapi Agent, now asks whether to merge them into one document (pages or photos of one paper document) or keep them separate. Merged files are stitched in order before reading, keeping every original file and page. Photos merge by default in Quick start.
While extracting, Quick start shows the workflow: prompt saved, waiting for a worker, reading the documents, checking the values, ready.
Extracted values show in the same popup with a Review button that opens that extraction on the Review page.
If the AI cannot suggest extraction fields, add them yourself.

releases.title: Contributor datasets use the workspace Default models
changes: New datasets created by contributors (Quick start or New dataset) now use the administrator's Default models instead of failing with an embedding-model error.
Model mapping for datasets is administrator-only again; contributors pick from the mapped models and the workspace Default chat model when they chat.
Quick start no longer shows a second 'Processing in background' panel on top of its own reading progress.
Quick start scrolls properly on tablets (the Continue button was cut off), and a new Enlarge button next to Close fills the window with it; your choice is remembered on that device.

releases.title: Contributor role from Keycloak
changes: New Keycloak role lapi-contributor: people who have it are Owner on every dataset and can create, delete and restore datasets, change dataset models and run dataset onboarding. Managing the workspace (users, teams, Access map, storage, settings, model registration, token usage) stays with administrators. Give it to everyone by adding it to the Keycloak realm's default roles; Lapi follows the change at the next sign-in, or within 5 minutes.

releases.title: Quick start and company sign-in
changes: New Quick start in Lapi's look: a short guided sheet that takes you through one complete workflow: choose or create a dataset, add a photo or files, watch them being read, then either ask your first question with sources, or pull out data. It is the first suggested step after the set-up questions, and the Add button on phones. Each step that sends data to an AI model asks for your consent first.
The Quick start is always on the Dashboard. On a computer it opens as a wide panel with a step list; on a phone it fills the screen.

Pull out data without writing a prompt: Lapi reads your document and suggests the fields to extract, you edit them or ask the AI to rewrite them ("add the due date"), then Lapi saves the prompt and runs the extraction.
Sign in with Microsoft or Google (and other providers) through Keycloak: one button each on the sign-in page, shown once they are set up in Keycloak.
When the chat model cannot answer, Lapi now says so instead of showing a server error.

releases.title: Hosted Keycloak starts
changes: Fix: hosted Keycloak now receives its start-up secrets when the container platform created their shared folder itself.

releases.title: Safer sign-in, set-up questions, phones and shortcuts
changes: You are signed out after 30 minutes without activity. Users & passwords shows My sessions: where you are signed in, with sign-out for any session; administrators can sign a person out everywhere.
Failed sign-ins are limited per person (5 in 15 minutes) and per address, so one person's mistakes no longer lock out everyone.
Password accounts can add an authenticator app; then signing in also needs a 6-digit code. Administrators can reset it when a phone is lost.
With Keycloak, Lapi re-checks every 5 minutes and signs people out when Keycloak does, so disabling someone or removing a role takes effect within minutes.
After the tour, two quick questions (what you want to do, where your knowledge is) lead to your first step and a "Your next steps" card on the Dashboard.
Phones: a bottom bar (Dashboard, Ask, Add knowledge, More), larger buttons and full-screen panels. Keyboard: press ? to see the shortcuts.

releases.title: Dataset roles, teams, Auditor and a 1-minute tour
changes: Each person or team now has a level on each dataset: Viewer (chat and read results), Editor (also upload, extract and review) or Owner (also the dataset's name, instructions and members). Existing access became Editor, so nobody lost what they could do.
Teams give dataset access to groups of people. Keycloak groups become teams automatically at sign-in; administrators can also create Lapi teams.
Dataset owners share their dataset from a new Members tab in Manage dataset, without being administrators.
New Auditor role (in Users & passwords, or the Keycloak role lapi-auditor): sees people and the Access map read-only, and no dataset content.
The Access map shows levels and teams, and OpenFGA checks every level and team grant.
Every API route now has a written access rule that is checked on each request; a route without one is refused.
A 1-minute animated tour of Connect · Unify · Ask opens once after your first sign-in and is always in About.

releases.title: HTTPS certificate saved for updates
changes: The web server that holds the HTTPS certificate now runs as the same user as Lapi, so Lapi can save the certificate and reuse it after updates.

releases.title: HTTPS certificate kept across updates
changes: The HTTPS certificate is now saved as soon as it is first obtained, so updating Lapi reuses it instead of requesting a new one.

releases.title: Lapi over HTTPS
changes: Lapi is served over HTTPS at https://lapi.92.4.94.96.sslip.io with a free Let's Encrypt certificate that renews itself. The old http://92.4.94.96 address redirects there, and sign-in cookies are now sent only over HTTPS.
The certificate is kept across deployments, so updating Lapi does not request a new one each time.

releases.title: Redesigned sign-in page
changes: The sign-in page now uses one blended background (blue, indigo, rose and peach) behind the Connect · Unify · Ask diagram, with a frosted-glass sign-in card instead of a separate white form and blue panel. The diagram itself is unchanged.

releases.title: Text-only files are indexed as their text
changes: A .pdf, .docx or image file that only holds text, such as a saved web link, is now indexed and extracted as that text instead of failing. Lapi never opens links found in a document. Files that are neither the named format nor text are still refused with the reason.

releases.title: OCR as a model use with its own Default
changes: Model Registration has an OCR checkbox in "Use for" (OpenAI and Gemini). Test connection sends a small sample image and checks the model reads it, so any OpenAI or Gemini model that accepts images (for example gpt-5.6-luna or gpt-6.1-terra) can do OCR, not only gpt-4o.
OCR has its own workspace Default. Each dataset now has four models: Chat, Extraction, Embedding and OCR; a dataset without its own OCR choice uses the OCR Default.

releases.title: Step-by-step connector guides
changes: Add knowledge now shows a plain-language, step-by-step guide for each storage connector (Amazon S3, Azure Blob Storage, OCI Object Storage, SharePoint, Google Drive and Google Cloud Storage): what you need, where to click in the provider's console, which value goes in which field, and how to fix each error Test connection can show.

releases.title: Image uploads read with OCR
changes: PNG, JPG and WEBP images can be uploaded, attached in Lapi Agent, merged with other files and imported from cloud connectors. Each image is read with the dataset's cloud OCR model (OpenAI gpt-4o / gpt-4o-mini or Gemini) and indexed as one page; PDF, DOCX, TXT and JSON stay supported.
OCR is now on in the OCI deployment, so scanned PDF pages are read too.

releases.title: Clear errors for files that are not really PDF or DOCX
changes: Uploads and cloud imports now check that a .pdf or .docx file really is a PDF or Word document, and say what it actually is (for example a saved web link, a web page or a renamed file) instead of failing later with "Processing failed".
Indexing a damaged or mislabelled file that was stored earlier now reports the same clear reason.

releases.title: Google Cloud Storage connector
changes: Add knowledge can now connect a Google Cloud Storage bucket (optionally limited to a folder prefix) with a read-only service-account key, browse it, and import and index PDF, DOCX, TXT and JSON files.

releases.title: Local reranker in the cloud deployment
changes: The API image now includes the pinned local reranker (ms-marco-MiniLM-L6-v2), and the OCI deployment turns it on, so chat and extraction no longer stop with "Chat reranking is unavailable".

releases.title: Keycloak sign-in, OpenFGA permissions and multi-use models
changes: People sign in with your organization's Keycloak. Their Lapi account is created at the first sign-in, and the Keycloak role lapi-administrator decides who is an administrator. Signing out of Lapi also signs out of Keycloak.
Lapi's own password sign-in remains only for local administrators, as a break-glass path when Keycloak is unavailable. Passwords and roles of Keycloak accounts are managed in Keycloak.
OpenFGA now answers every permission check: who administers Lapi and which datasets each person may open. If OpenFGA cannot answer, access is refused rather than granted.

Model Registration has a Use for choice instead of a single Category. One model can serve Chat and Extraction together, and each role can be a workspace Default on its own. Ticking Embedding as well also saves an embedding registration of the same model and connection; Test Connection checks every ticked use.

releases.title: Choose each model's API
changes: Model Registration has an API field for Chat and Extraction models. OpenAI-compatible and Azure OpenAI models can use Chat Completions or the Responses API; Anthropic, Bedrock, Vertex, OCI and Ollama show the one chat API they offer.

With Responses, models such as gpt-6.1-terra can call Lapi's tools while reasoning. Tool steps, chat answers, extraction and OCR all use the chosen API; Responses answers arrive in one piece rather than streamed, and OpenAI keeps no copy.

releases.title: Model tests explain provider errors
changes: When Test Connection fails in Model Registration, the message now includes the provider's own reason (for example an unsupported parameter or API), with any key removed. Errors during normal use still never show provider text, which can echo private requests.

releases.title: A redesigned sign-in page
changes: Sign-in has a calm white form column (larger fields, a gradient Sign in button, a note that sessions end after 12 hours) beside a brand-blue panel that says what Lapi does: "Ask your data. Get answers you can trust."

The Connect -> Unify -> Ask diagram is redrawn for the blue panel with fewer, larger elements: glass source tiles, a white knowledge core with the Lapi mark, and a Lapi Agent chat card with numbered citations and matching source chips.

Three facts sit under the diagram: cited answers, governed access and self-hosting. On phones the form comes first and the panel keeps its words; the diagram is hidden where its labels would be too small to read.

releases.title: Oracle vector table at start-up; sign-in over HTTP
changes: When Oracle is both the database and the vector store through deployment settings, Lapi creates its vector table at start-up, so readiness checks, indexing and chat work without first activating Oracle on the Storage screen.
Signing in and using Lapi over plain HTTP no longer fails with "crypto.randomUUID is not a function": request IDs fall back to crypto.getRandomValues where the browser hides randomUUID.

releases.title: Containers on OCI, no setup token
changes: Lapi runs as containers on OCI Container Instances behind a load balancer, with no VM: data and vectors in the lapidb Autonomous AI Database, files and Lapi's own settings in Object Storage, and the local Ollama models alongside.

The setup screen and its bootstrap token are gone. The first administrator is created on the server (create-admin, or once at start-up from an OCI Vault secret); the sign-in page says when none exists yet.
The key that encrypts saved model keys and passwords, and the database password, can come from OCI Vault instead of server configuration.

releases.title: One knowledge base
changes: All datasets now share one knowledge index built with the workspace Default embedding model: each document is embedded once, and the index catalog lives in the database instead of files on one server.

Model Registration marks one Default model per role (Chat, Extraction, Embedding). Datasets use the workspace Default unless they choose their own Chat or Extraction model; only models with a passing connection test can become Default.

Changing the Embedding Default asks for explicit confirmation, deletes the knowledge index straight away and rebuilds it; a banner on every page shows how many documents are reindexed and lets administrators retry failures. Chat answers from documents already reindexed and says the index is still building.
When existing datasets use different embedding models, an administrator chooses one Default before the shared index is built.

releases.title: Agentic chat, skills and memory
changes: Lapi Agent can run as an agentic chat (LAPI_CHAT_MODE router, agentic or auto). With a cloud function-calling model such as Gemini it plans, calls several read tools in parallel, reads more evidence per step and answers in one loop; the local model keeps the routed chat.

Every factual sentence must cite a source read for this answer, and its numbers, dates and names must appear in that source. A failing answer is revised once; anything still unsupported is removed and the answer says how many statements were removed.
Follow-up questions understand earlier turns (text and citation IDs only), and answers show the agent's plan, source snippets and up to three suggested follow-up questions.

New Skills & memory page: built-in and custom skills (/skill), dataset answer instructions with versions (/instructions, /optimize with a Save card), model prompting guides, and a private memory note with 90-day question history that you can edit, switch off or clear.
Token usage is recorded for every model call with dated prices per model; each answer shows its tokens and approximate cost per step, and administrators get a Token usage report with CSV export.
Model Registration has a typed parameter form per stage (Chat answer, Tool steps, Extraction, Optimize) with documented Lapi defaults, suggested values, per-stage test prompts and a change history.
Claude and Bedrock prompt caching and an OpenAI prompt cache key keep the stable agent instructions cached between turns.

releases.title: Connect · Unify · Ask
changes: The Lapi tagline is now Connect · Unify · Ask: the banner's middle step reads Unify, and the sign-in card uses the same tagline.
The sign-in form no longer sits in a card: it blends into a light page background that is cleaner behind the form and softly tinted blue and orange at the edges.

releases.title: Horizontal sign-in banner
changes: The sign-in banner now flows left to right: data sources on the left, the knowledge core in the middle and a cited answer on the right.
The Lapi mark sits at the centre of the knowledge core, circled by a slowly turning ring of vector points; the banner is wider and landscape.

releases.title: Lapi brand
changes: New Lapi brand: an L with a speech-bubble P (ask) and an orange answer dot, from Laya (harmony) and Poorni (complete).
The mark on white is used in the header, sign-in card and banner; the blue-tile version is the Lapi Agent icon, browser tab icon and app icon.
A custom lowercase lapi wordmark, with an orange dot on the i, leads the sign-in banner.

releases.title: Lapi LP monogram
changes: New Lapi LP monogram: the L and P share one stem, with a white L foot, a light-orange P bowl and a knowledge node, on a blue tile.
The monogram is the Lapi Agent icon everywhere (chat, workflow tracks, activity capsule) and is used in the header, sign-in card, password recovery, the sign-in banner and the browser tab icon.

releases.title: Connect · Vectorize · Ask sign-in banner
changes: The sign-in banner tells the Lapi story in three steps: Connect data from anywhere (documents, databases, cloud storage, apps and APIs, sheets, email), Vectorize it into one unified knowledge base, and Ask questions that come back with sources.
The banner is drawn in the Lapi palette with flowing blue and orange dots, scales sharply on every screen, and pauses its motion when reduced motion is requested.
The sign-in tagline is now Connect · Vectorize · Ask.

releases.title: Lapi colours: white, blue and light orange
changes: Every screen uses the Lapi palette: white surfaces, blue for primary actions and headers, and light orange accents.
The sidebar is white with a blue selected item and an orange marker; page headers, workflow tracks and the Agent progress capsule use one blue band with a warm orange glow.
The sign-in page is light, with the banner shown as a framed card beside a white form.

releases.title: Lapi: new name and separate deployment
changes: The application is now Lapi: sign-in page, logo, header, Agent, About, code folders, Python packages, settings and environment names all use Lapi.
Lapi runs on its own Always Free OCI resources: a dedicated compartment, network, server and Autonomous Database.

releases.title: One workflow track everywhere
changes: Every workflow uses the navy phase track: Agent onboarding, tool steps and prompt progress, uploads, extraction and document processing, Files & processing, and storage and connection operations.
Each step keeps its name and status visible, finished steps fill the line, dots flow into the running step and the running step carries the Lapi shield; phones show a vertical list.

releases.title: Agent workflow and dataset editing
changes: While Lapi Agent works, a navy capsule shows the Lapi shield in a spinning ring with the current step, such as Searching knowledge or Writing the answer.

The answer workflow groups its steps into four phases: Understand request, Find evidence, Write answer and Check & save. It opens inline under the agent header as a navy phase track with the agent shield on the live phase; Show all steps keeps every actual step and its timing.

Edit any dataset from Datasets, or type /Manage in Lapi Agent: rename it, change its description or active state, its models, documents and prompts. In the Agent the dataset card stays in the conversation, and Upload or Extract start /Upload or /Extract there.
Administrators can rename and describe datasets without changing their models, documents, prompts or access.

releases.title: Jobs monitoring
changes: Jobs & activity becomes a monitoring view: running and queued work, failures that need attention, jobs completed in the last 24 hours and the average time per completed job.
Each job shows who started it, its dataset, when it started, how long it took and its progress. Administrators see usernames; other users see You or Another user.
Activity by person shows each person's running, failed and completed jobs; select a person, job type or search text to filter the list.

releases.title: Redesigned workspace screens
changes: Lapi Agent opens as a workspace: a conversation rail with recent chats, a wider thread and a context panel, with workflow cards to start Onboard, Upload, Extract or Re-extract.

Agent commands now start with / (/Onboard, /Upload, /Extract, /ReExtract); a leading @ is still understood. While work runs, the agent icon shows the live step: searching, reranking, writing, checking citations, uploading, indexing or extracting.

Every workspace screen opens with a brand page band and summary counts: Dataset, Prompt, Extract, Review, Jobs (now status tabs and cards), Model Registration, Model Mapping (with a dataset quick-pick that names missing models), Users and Files & processing.

Click any Need attention count or failed status to open a pop-up listing each affected file with its processing stages, the stored error, what to do next, Retry and links to the screen that fixes it. Administrator-only fixes tell other users to ask an administrator.

Buttons follow one compact standard across the workspace: the same size and shape, a brand-blue primary action, white secondary actions and red-outlined delete. New extraction moves from the top bar into the Extract and Review pages.
About shows the current version, a worked example from predefined prompts to reviewed fields and the golden copy, and a collapsible version history.

releases.title: Dashboard landing and Add knowledge
changes: Open Dashboard on a brand overview: greeting, an Ask box, summary counts from loaded accessible records, dataset cards and Sources. Asking gives the chat the full page; Back to overview keeps the conversation.

Quickly add or remove datasets from the Ask box, and choose individual files in a redesigned Add Dataset Knowledge picker. New knowledge in chat is announced with suggested questions; nothing runs until you ask.

Add new knowledge: any signed-in user can connect Amazon S3, Azure Blob Storage, OCI Object Storage, SharePoint or Google Drive to a dataset they can access, test it, browse and Vectorize up to 20 files. Connections are private to their owner; administrators see all.

Vectorize indexes copies with the dataset embedding model and publishes them to chat before showing Ready to ask. Extraction and review stay separate. Credentials are encrypted and never shown again; wrong details get specific guidance.
Read-only snapshots: cloud files are never changed, and later remote changes, deletions and permissions are not synchronized.

releases.title: Animated sign-in
changes: Show the unchanged Lapi banner on its own edge navy, with dots that travel along the banner's model and knowledge-source connector lines into the shield.
Blend the sign-in side from navy into blue and violet with a slow horizontal shift, drifting cyan and violet light and a frosted form card showing the Lapi shield, name and tagline.
Rotate the banner's five platform pillars beneath the form. All motion is horizontal and stops when the device requests reduced motion.
Place the sign-in form before the artwork in reading order and on mobile. Labels, autocomplete, focus, password visibility, recovery and authentication behavior are unchanged.

releases.title: Reliable file catalog refresh
changes: Show saved indexing and model mapping status without contacting model services while listing files.
Keep a slow file-list response visible by preventing overlapping timed refreshes.
Keep live model validation on retry and extraction submissions, and preserve complete document cleanup.

releases.title: Admin files and processing
changes: List application source files and their OCI/local storage, indexing, OCR and extraction status under Manage workspace.
Retry indexing and start new extractions with current dataset model mappings.
Preview permanent document deletion and remove related originals, revisions, OCR, indexes, result files and affected chats/workflows with resumable cleanup.
Include visible Save and New extraction buttons from the preceding prepared release.

releases.title: Visible extraction and Save actions
changes: Start a new extraction directly from the Extract screen with a labeled button.
Keep New extraction text visible on Review and on small screens.
Show labeled Save buttons in Model Mapping, model registration and settings instead of tick-only controls.

releases.title: Rerun with current mapped models
changes: Resolve current dataset models for each new Re-extract, prompt Resume and Reindex submission.
Rebuild scanned source indexes when the mapped OCR model changes before Review re-extraction.
Prevent historical retries from replaying outdated model mappings or damaging successful indexes/results.
Keep accepted jobs pinned and preserve earlier results and original files.

releases.title: Cloud OCR page budgets
changes: Use the selected OpenAI model's registered context limit for OCR.
Estimate GPT-4o and GPT-4o Mini image tokens with their cloud tile rules, preserving original pixels.
Keep cloud-only OCR selection and reject pages that exceed the registered model budget before inference.

releases.title: Cloud-only dataset OCR
changes: Offer only compatible OpenAI and Gemini OCR models in dataset Model Mapping.
Automatic OCR uses the compatible cloud extraction default, with no local model fallback.
Reject local OCR selections and give a clear cloud model selection message when scanned content needs OCR.

releases.title: Choose OCR per dataset
changes: Choose a compatible OpenAI or Gemini OCR model independently in Model Mapping, alongside Embedding, Chat and Extraction.
Keep Automatic provider routing or explicitly use the configured local OCR service.
Apply the choice to new indexing jobs, retain queued work and embedding settings, and reindex existing documents to read their images again.

releases.title: OpenAI OCR for cloud datasets
changes: Read scanned PDF pages and embedded Word images with the mapped GPT-4o or GPT-4o Mini extraction model.
Disclose OpenAI image transmission and pin the saved model and credential version for each job.
Keep embeddings separate, retain original documents and transcription checks, and report cloud failures without falling back to local Ollama.

releases.title: Summarize selected dataset knowledge
changes: Treat broad knowledge-base summaries as complete read-only questions scoped to the selected dataset or documents.
Route short summaries through the model instead of assuming a previous extraction answer.
Preserve hybrid retrieval, reranking, evidence citations and separate processing confirmations.

releases.title: Multiple models per dataset
changes: Enable several Chat and Extraction models per dataset while retaining one default for each role.
Keep enabled alternatives when a default changes; protect selected defaults from being disabled.
Preserve embedding selection, index generation and existing mapping concurrency checks.

releases.title: Reliable Agent source routing
changes: Use strict OpenAI and Azure routing arguments, with nullable optional values normalized before canonical validation.
Separate original document questions, semantic search and saved extraction filters so content questions retrieve indexed passages.
Keep dataset/topic names out of filename filters, preserve selected access scope, and retain hybrid search, reranking and citation validation.

releases.title: OpenAI Agent routing compatibility
changes: Fix OpenAI and Azure OpenAI Agent routing by declaring each route alternative as an object-shaped function.
Validate returned arguments against the selected branch and canonical route, and retain provider function names when continuing a tool conversation.
Preserve dataset access, hybrid retrieval, reranking, cited answer validation and existing model registrations.

releases.title: Direct Claude for Agent chat
changes: Register a direct Anthropic Claude Chat model using its API key, exact model ID and optional workspace ID.
Test native function calling before saving, map the model to datasets and select it for Agent or Dataset Knowledge Chat.
Preserve scoped knowledge retrieval, reranking, citation checks and existing Embedding, Extraction and processing models.

releases.title: A roomier three-panel Dashboard
changes: Arrange authorized datasets on the left, Dataset Knowledge Chat in the centre and Sources on the right.
Keep dataset and source panels visible when selecting knowledge; expand chat only when requested.
Use separate Datasets, Knowledge Chat and Sources views on smaller screens while preserving the conversation and draft.

releases.title: Restore the light sign-in background
changes: Keep the sign-in page white-toned with subtle blue and cyan background accents matching the supplied banner.
Preserve the banner image, removed duplicate sign-in branding and supplied shield throughout the application.

releases.title: Use the supplied shield for Lapi Agent
changes: Use the supplied Lapi shield wherever the shared Agent identity appears: navigation, welcome screens, chat replies, workflow guidance and the floating shortcut.
Archive the previous Agent artwork; preserve existing icon sizes, accessible labels, chat behavior and workflow status icons.

releases.title: A blended sign-in background
changes: Remove the repeated Lapi logo and tagline above the sign-in heading.
Match the sign-in page background to the supplied bannerâ€™s navy tones without changing, cropping, fading or blending the banner image.

releases.title: Lapi platform branding
changes: Use the supplied Lapi shield logo in the sign-in page, workspace header, navigation, password recovery and browser icon.
Display the supplied platform banner in full beside sign-in on desktop and below the form on mobile.
Archive the previous artwork and keep this frontend branding change independently reversible in Git.

releases.title: A cleaner Dataset Knowledge Chat input
changes: Remove the inner rectangular border, focus outline and background from the Dashboard chat input.
Keep the rounded outer composer focus indicator and existing keyboard, draft and chat behavior.

releases.title: Explore metadata as a connected graph
changes: Explore records and expand or collapse their saved connections in place, using the existing access-scoped metadata API.
Arrange the graph as a network or lineage; pin nodes to preserve their positions during automatic layout.
Highlight neighbouring records, filter entity types, toggle relationship labels, zoom with the wheel and inspect parallel links separately.
Keep mouse, touch and keyboard node movement, scoped counts and read-only processing boundaries. No Neo4j service or paid cloud feature is required.

releases.title: Arrange metadata relationship nodes
changes: Drag each category or record node independently with a mouse, touch or pen; connections and labels follow its position.
Pan the background, zoom, fit the arranged graph to the screen or restore its starting layout with the reset icon.
Use arrow keys to adjust a focused node, Shift for larger steps and Home to reset that node. Enter or Space opens its details.
Keep separate arrangements for scoped desktop and mobile views while the explorer is open, including across list switches and refresh. No metadata or model calls are changed.

releases.title: Compact chat layout controls
changes: Use icons for showing or hiding Sources and expanding or restoring the Dashboard chat layout.
Keep descriptive tooltips, accessible labels and larger mobile touch targets for the layout controls.
Preserve the selected knowledge, draft and conversation when changing the layout.

releases.title: Give Dataset Knowledge Chat more room
changes: Expand Dataset Knowledge Chat after indexed knowledge is included through the picker, dataset cards, checkboxes or drag and drop.
Collapse dataset cards, Sources and guidance around the conversation. Keep the knowledge summary and Add Dataset Knowledge available.
Inspect sources or restore the Dashboard without resetting the chat draft, selected knowledge or conversation. Focus the composer when chat opens; send no question automatically.
Fit the expanded conversation and composer within the desktop and mobile workspace.

releases.title: Explore metadata relationships
changes: Open Metadata Relationships from the Dashboard Knowledge Source header, on demand.
Explore access-scoped datasets, documents, saved extraction runs, prompt versions, review revisions and mapped models.
Inspect records and relationships with dataset selection, search, graph/list views, zoom, pan and mobile details.
Lapi blue and navy relationship graph on a light canvas, with matching controls and record details.
Read-only metadata inspection preserves Dashboard chat and processing workflows; no model calls, graph database or schema changes are required.

releases.title: Dataset knowledge, within easy reach
changes: Add Dataset Knowledge stays visible in a sticky toolbar while sources and chat scroll, including when Sources is collapsed.
Combine multiple datasets using the Include dataset checkboxes or the indexed-file picker.
Drag dataset cards into Sources to include their accessible indexed files, preserving other selected sources.
Find the current version and version-by-version feature history on the About screen.

releases.title: Lapi baseline and Dashboard foundation
changes: Document onboarding, uploads, model mappings, extraction, review and the original Lapi Agent.
Dashboard with dataset cards, permitted Unified Knowledge sources and a separate read-only Dataset Knowledge Chat.
Chat opens on demand. Greetings and self-contained general questions use the selected model without knowledge lookup; dataset questions retain retrieval, reranking and citations.
Compact Connections footer with model hosting details. Original Dataset onboarding remains in its existing workspace.
